q: A Draft Para is received by the General Manager. The accounts wing is preparing the reply and three weeks have already passed. What is the correct course for the reply?

options.A: Send the reply directly to Audit without any vetting, at any time within three months
options.B: Furnish the reply within 6 weeks, with the reply vetted by the PFA
options.C: Convert the Draft Para into a Provisional Para before replying
options.D: Wait for the PAC to call for the reply and then respond within 2 weeks

q: Audit receives the reply to a Draft Para but is not satisfied with the explanation furnished. What happens next in the chain?

options.A: An Action Taken Note is prepared immediately
options.B: The para is dropped automatically
options.C: The matter goes straight to the PAC for personal evidence
options.D: The Draft Para is converted into a Provisional Para, for which the reply time is 2 weeks

q: Even after the Provisional Para stage, Audit remains dissatisfied with the administration's reply. What is the correct next step?

options.A: The Provisional Para becomes an Audit Para and forms part of the CAG's Annual Report laid before Parliament
options.B: The para is returned to the unit as an Inspection Report Part II item
options.C: The para is settled by the passage of time
options.D: The PFA closes the para on his own authority

q: The Appropriation Accounts of a railway show that actual expenditure under a grant has exceeded the final grant. What is required to deal with this excess?

options.A: It is adjusted against a saving under another grant without informing Parliament
options.B: It is written off by the Member (Finance) in the Finance Accounts
options.C: It is treated as a surrender and closed in the Traffic Account
options.D: It requires regularisation by Parliament through an excess grant after PAC examination

q: In October, a division foresees that a large part of a grant will remain unspent because a work will not be completed this year. What should it do with the expected saving?

options.A: Retain it till the close of the year and surrender it thereafter
options.B: Surrender the saving as soon as it is foreseen, by the prescribed dates
options.C: Spend it on another work without any re-appropriation
options.D: Keep it as a reserve for the next financial year

q: Expenditure has exceeded the provision under one head, but there is a saving under another head in the same grant. No valid re-appropriation was made in time. Can the excess be treated as cured?

options.A: Yes, because savings and excesses in the same grant always cancel each other
options.B: Yes, if the PFA certifies the position after the year ends
options.C: No, an excess is not cured by a saving elsewhere unless a valid re-appropriation was made in time
options.D: Yes, if the amount is shown in Annexure J

q: An objection raised in Inspection Report Part II remains unsettled and Audit considers the matter serious. Following the graded hierarchy, towards which stage will it be escalated?

options.A: Towards Part I, then Special Letter and Draft Para if still unresolved
options.B: Directly to an Action Taken Report
options.C: To a Draft Observation Slip, as a lower stage
options.D: To the Finance Accounts for certification only

q: The PAC takes up an important Audit Para and wants first-hand evidence on the facts. From whom does the PAC obtain personal evidence in such cases?

options.A: Only from the station staff who booked the transactions
options.B: Only from the CAG's audit inspectors
options.C: Only from the Traffic Inspectors of Accounts
options.D: From senior officers - GMs and Board Members

q: After PAC examination of an Audit Para, the administration must show what action has been taken - recovery made, procedure corrected and responsibility fixed. At which stage is responsibility fixed at officers' level?

options.A: At the Draft Para stage
options.B: At the Action Taken Note (ATN) stage
options.C: At the Inspection Report Part II stage
options.D: At the Draft Observation Slip stage

q: A unit replies to a long-outstanding audit objection by saying that the objection is very old and should therefore be treated as dropped. What is the correct position?

options.A: The objection lapses automatically after three years
options.B: The objection can be dropped by the audited office itself
options.C: An objection is disposed of only when Audit is satisfied with the reply and evidence, not by the passage of time
options.D: Old objections are transferred to the Finance Accounts

q: While explaining variations in the Appropriation Accounts, an accounts officer compares only the Original Grant with the Actual Expenditure. What is wrong with this approach?

options.A: Variation is explained between the Original Grant plus Supplementary Grant and the Actual Expenditure
options.B: Variation should be explained only against the Supplementary Grant
options.C: Variation should be explained only against the Final Grant surrender figure
options.D: No explanation of variation is needed in the Appropriation Accounts

q:
Consider the following statements about the Appropriation Accounts:
1. They are prepared by the accounting authorities, not by the CAG.
2. The CAG audits and certifies them.
3. The Railway Appropriation Accounts are signed by the Member (Finance) and the CAG.
4. They are prepared in thousands of rupees.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1, 3 and 4 only

q:
Consider the following statements about the CAG:
1. The CAG is appointed by the President.
2. The CAG can be removed only in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. The CAG's salary is voted annually by Parliament.
4. The form of Union and State accounts is prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.B: 1, 2 and 4 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 2 and 4 only

q:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It has not more than 22 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The term of office of its members is one year.
3. It is a Standing Committee of Parliament under the control of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
4. The CAG acts as its friend, philosopher and guide.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.D: 2, 3 and 4 only

q:
Consider the following statements about the graded hierarchy of audit objections:
1. Draft Observation Slips stand below Inspection Report / Audit Notes Part II.
2. Part I items are more serious than Part II items.
3. A Special Letter stands above a Draft Para in the hierarchy.
4. An Audit Para is the highest stage, forming part of the CAG's Report.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1, 2 and 4 only
options.C: 2 and 4 only
options.D: 1 and 3 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Finance Accounts show the receipts and disbursements of the Government as a whole, including the public debt position.
2. Appropriation Accounts compare the final grant with actual expenditure, grant by grant.
3. Appropriation Accounts include the Profit and Loss Account of the railway undertaking.
4. Both Finance Accounts and Appropriation Accounts are audited and certified by the CAG.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1 and 4 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 4 only
options.D: 2 and 3 only

q: In the compilation of the Appropriation Accounts, Annexure J represents which of the following?

options.A: Persistent savings and excesses
options.B: Unsanctioned expenditure
options.C: Important Misclassifications
options.D: Defects in budgeting

q: In which year was Railway Audit separated from Accounts?
Theme-based audit was introduced by the CAG in which year?
At the zonal level, who is the head of the Audit Department?

options.A: The Principal Financial Adviser
options.B: The General Manager
options.C: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.D: The Director General / Principal Director of Audit

q: The audit that culminates in the CAG's certificate on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts is known as which type of audit?

options.A: Performance audit
options.B: Certification (financial attest) audit
options.C: Propriety audit
options.D: Theme-based audit

q: Which one of the following statements about Railway Audit is NOT correct?

options.A: The scope and extent of Railway Audit is determined by the CAG
options.B: Audit functions for Railways are controlled at the apex by the Deputy C&AG (Railways)
options.C: Railway Audit works under the supervision of the Principal Financial Adviser
options.D: Audit presents a free and fair view as a constitutional requirement

q: Which one of the following statements about the Draft Para / Provisional Para procedure is NOT correct?

options.A: The time limit for reply to a Provisional Para is 6 weeks
options.B: The Draft Para is sent by the DG/PDA to the General Manager
options.C: Advance copies of the Draft Para are endorsed to the PFA and the PHOD
options.D: The reply to a Draft Para must be vetted by the PFA

q: Which one of the following statements about the PAC follow-up cycle is NOT correct?

options.A: The cycle runs ATN, then ATS, then ATR
options.B: ATN stands for Action Taken Note
options.C: ATR stands for Action Taken Report
options.D: The cycle runs ATR first, then ATS, and ATN last

q:
Assertion (A): Responsibility for an audit para is fixed at officers' level at the Action Taken Note stage.
Reason (R): The ATN is the audited reply showing what has been done on each para or recommendation - recovery made, procedure corrected and responsibility fixed.

options.A: Both A and R are false
options.B: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true
